# Volume 3 — Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Having arrived unexpectedly around the corner of the porch, Hugh stated, “This afternoon, I want to invite you to take a walk like we used to, traveling past hills rich with aromatic scents and across autumn forests. What if we make our way to the garden belonging to Dinah Wren?””
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0000 }

Nell, who was seated upon the stone step with a light, sheer, green material filling her lap, raised her eyes somewhat vacant-eyed.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0001 }

“Oh, how I desire to do so,” she uttered with deliberation, “yet it is truly impossible for me, Hugh. You are aware that I must attend the wedding of Alice Penhallow later today. This gown requires some alterations from me, and once those are completed, my preparation for the event must begin. I am terribly grieved. My heart would delight in joining you.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0002 }

“Well, are you able to leave tomorrow afternoon, instead?” inquired Hugh, who did not seem particularly let down.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0003 }

“Indeed, that is my belief.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0004 }

“Under those circumstances I will hurry home right away so I can handle a task I would need to perform tomorrow if I did not. Thus Alice Penhallow gets married this evening. You get three weddings during a single summer, Nell—Cressy’s, Alice’s, and Odette’s. Odette will not be forgiven by me for leaving me off the guest list for her wedding.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0005 }

“Considering the massive Pullen family who required invitations, you truly cannot hold it against her. They could barely fit inside the house. My own invitation came solely through being Odette’s long-standing friend—from Odette’s perspective, anyway. Mrs. Gorham invited me, I suspect, so that I might witness the ultimate magnificence of Odette.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0006 }

“Was it really the case that her body was covered in so many diamonds that differentiating between the jewels and Odette was impossible?”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0007 }

A laugh came from Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0008 }

“She definitely had on quite a lot. Between all those diamonds, the white satin, the tulle, the lace, the roses, and the orange blossoms, precise little Odette was nearly hidden from view. Nevertheless, she felt extremely happy, as did Mr. Inglis—and Mrs. Gorham as well.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0009 }

“Are those the clothes you plan on wearing this evening?” Hugh inquired, gazing downward at the frills and fluffs.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0010 }

“Indeed. Does it not look lovely? Furthermore, starflowers will adorn my hair. They are growing all over The Whispering Wood during this summer.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0011 }

Hugh was abruptly struck by an image of Nell, dressed in a ruffled green dress, her untouched curved throat and arms emerging from the garment, while pale stars gleamed in the twists of her reddish hair. The mental picture caused his breathing to falter. Nevertheless, he pivoted away with airiness.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0012 }

“Indeed, I will come up tomorrow. I hope your time tonight is enjoyable.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0013 }

Nell watched him walk away with long strides, and released a sigh. Hugh was amiable—extremely amiable—much too amiable. Subsequent to his restoration to health, he had visited Grey Shutters frequently, and a portion of their former fellowship had been restored. However, it no longer contented Nell. When set against the rose of love, friendship's bloom seemed washed-out and lacking fragrance. Furthermore, Nell had once more started to question whether Hugh currently experienced any emotion for her beyond friendship. The brilliant assurance she felt on that enraptured morning had dimmed in the ordinary light of an ordinary day. A wretched dread tormented her that her error was impossible to correct. It was entirely possible that Rowena was the one Hugh actually loved. It might be that he was even betrothed to her. Nell attempted to banish every disturbing expectation from her soul, and adapt to a destiny in which labor and aspiration would have to substitute for love. As an instructor, she was capable of doing worthwhile, if not grand, work; while the favor her modest drawings were starting to receive in some editorial offices boded well for her developing writerly ambitions. Yet—yet—Nell lifted her green gown and let out another sigh.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0014 }

Upon Hugh's arrival the following afternoon, Nell was expecting him, looking as fresh as dawn and as fair as a star, despite the previous night's festivities. She had put on a green dress—different from her wedding attire, but a former dress that Hugh had singled out as a favorite during a Wexcombe reception. This precise hue of green highlighted the deep tones of her hair, the star-like gray of her eyes, and her skin's delicate, iris-like complexion. Walking beside her on a shaded woodland trail, Hugh looked at her from the corner of his eye and felt she was more beautiful than ever before. Stealing occasional side glances at Hugh, Nell reflected on how significantly older he appeared after his sickness. He seemed to have relinquished his youth permanently.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0015 }

The weather was splendid and the route was splendid. Nell felt a slight regret when they arrived at Dinah Wren’s garden and took a seat on the ancient bench. Yet that place possessed splendour as well—just as splendid as it was on the distant day of the Golden Picnic, when Isolde and Odette and Honora and she had discovered it. At that time, narcissus and violets made it lovely; currently, golden rod had lit its fairy torches in the corners and asters scattered blue spots across it. From the birch valley, the brook's call drifted up through the trees carrying every bit of its former fascination; the purr of the sea saturated the soft air; further out lay fields bordered by fences that multi-summer suns had bleached to a silvery gray, alongside sprawling hills draped in the shadows of autumn clouds; as the west wind blew, former dreams came back.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0016 }

“It seems to me,” Nell uttered in a quiet voice, “that ‘the land where dreams come true’ lies within the blue haze over there, past that small valley.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0017 }

“Are there any dreams you have not fulfilled, Nell?” Hugh asked.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0018 }

Nell’s heart began to throb furiously because of a particular quality in his voice—a quality that she had not detected since that wretched night in the orchard at Tabby’s Place. She replied, however, in an airy manner.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0019 }

“Naturally. Everyone does. Having all our wishes realized would not be good for us. If there remained nothing for us to imagine, we might as well be dead. How wonderful a fragrance the setting sun is drawing out of those ferns and asters. It would be my desire to view scents in addition to smelling them. They would be exceptionally lovely, I am certain.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0020 }

Such a distraction failed to derail Hugh.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0021 }

“I possess a dream,” he uttered unhurriedly. “It is a dream I continue to hold, even if I have frequently felt it might never be realized. In this dream, there is a residence containing a burning hearth, a dog alongside a cat, the sound of friends approaching—and you!”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0022 }

Nell wished to express herself, yet no words came to her. A surge of happiness washed over her like a wave. She felt nearly terrified by it.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0023 }

“Nell, I posed a question to you more than two years back. Should I repeat that inquiry today, will your response be any different?”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0024 }

Nell remained unable to utter a word. Nevertheless, she raised her gaze, which glowed with the entire romantic ecstasy of innumerable generations, and briefly met his eyes. No further response was needed by him.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0025 }

They remained in the ancient garden while the evening shadows, which were as lovely as the dusk of Eden surely was, slowly enveloped the place. So many matters required discussion and remembrance—words uttered and actions taken, things overheard, ideas conceived, emotions experienced, and points misinterpreted.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0026 }

“I believed Rowena Calder was the object of your affection,” Nell said to him, speaking with as much disapproval as though she had not provided him with complete cause to assume that Cyril Lisle had her own love.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0027 }

Hugh uttered a youthful laugh.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0028 }

“Rowena was betrothed to a person in her native town. This was known to me, and she was aware that I knew it. Upon his graduation, her brother informed me that his sister intended to come to Portmaris the following winter for music study, and he requested that I pay her some attention, since she was unacquainted with anyone and would feel quite lonely. Therefore, I obliged. Subsequently, I grew fond of Rowena on her own merits. She ranks among the finest girls I have ever encountered. I was mindful that campus rumors attributed a romantic involvement to us. It was of no concern to me. For a period back then, after you informed me that you could never care for me, Nell, nothing held much significance for me. There was no other person—for me, there could never be anyone but you. My love for you has endured from the moment you shattered your slate across my head at school.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0029 }

“I fail to understand how your love for me could persist while I behaved like such a silly girl,” Nell remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0030 }

“Indeed, I attempted to cease,” Hugh admitted openly, “not owing to a belief that you were what you term yourself, but since I was convinced my prospects vanished once Lisle arrived. Yet I was unable to—and it is impossible to express the impact it had on me over those two years when I thought you would wed him, and received weekly reports from various meddlers stating the public declaration of your betrothal was imminent. My belief persisted until a wonderful day while I was convalescing following the fever. A missive arrived for me from Cressy Lindsay—or more accurately, Cressy Hale—where she informed me that you and Cyril were actually not involved, and suggested I ‘try again.’ Truly, the physician was astonished by how quickly I got better following that.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0031 }

Nell giggled, and after that she shuddered.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0032 }

“I will always remember that evening when I believed you were passing away, Hugh. Oh, I was aware—I was aware right then—and I believed the time had already run out.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0033 }

“However, it was not, my love. Ah, Nell, does this not compensate for all else? Let us make a vow to reserve this date forever to pure loveliness throughout our existence because of the present it has granted us.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0034 }

“It’s the anniversary of our joy,” Nell murmured. “This old garden belonging to Dinah Wren has always been beloved by me, and from now on it will be even more precious.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0035 }

“However, Nell, you must be prepared for a lengthy wait,” Hugh remarked mournfully. “Three years will pass before my studies in medicine are complete. Furthermore, even at that point, marble halls and diamond sunbursts will not be ours.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0036 }

A laugh came from Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0037 }

“Sunbursts and marble halls are not what I desire. My only wish is for you. As you can tell, I have just as little shame regarding this as Cressy. While marble halls and sunbursts might be perfectly fine, lacking them offers greater ‘scope for imagination’. Furthermore, the period of waiting is unimportant. Happy is what we will be, as we wait and work for one another—and dream. Oh, sweet dreams are what we will have now.”
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0038 }

Hugh pulled her near to his side and pressed his lips to hers. Afterwards, they strolled back to their house as one during the twilight, reigning as king and queen within love's matrimonial domain, treading meandering trails edged by the most fragrant blossoms to ever flower, and traversing enchanted fields swept by breezes of expectation and remembrance.
{: #nw-v03-c41-p0039 }
